name: Phrasal Exclamation with What
pattern: independent NP[exclamative what + optional a/an + Nom]

entry.name: Phrasal Exclamation with What
entry.pattern: independent NP[exclamative what + optional a/an + Nom]

1.definition: Expresses an affective evaluation through an apt nominal description.

projection.target: The singular count example includes a, whereas What lovely weather! does not. The independent pattern needs no finite predication to convey the evaluation.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: What a mess!
curious.summary: What plus a noun description can express a feeling about something, with no verb at all.
curious.body:
What a mess! expresses a reaction. There's no verb and no complete statement, yet the feeling about the mess comes through clearly. The words that follow what describe the thing aptly and give the speaker's evaluation.

In What a mess!, the word a comes between what and the singular noun. Not every case has it: What lovely weather! doesn't. The pattern needs no verb to carry its meaning.

This dictionary marks this account as provisional.
curious.try: React to something in the room using What a ... or What ... Does your reaction need a verb?

teacher.summary: Helps explain verbless what-exclamations as a way to evaluate something.
teacher.explain: The pattern is an independent noun phrase with exclamative what, an optional a or an, and a nominal. It expresses an affective evaluation through an apt nominal description. The singular count example includes a, as in What a mess!, whereas What lovely weather! does not. The independent pattern needs no finite predication to convey the evaluation. This dictionary relates it to exclamative words and clauses and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: This dictionary treats what here as an exclamative form in a noun phrase.
watch_for: A learner might look for a verb in What a mess!, when none is needed.
A learner might add a before lovely weather, though this dictionary's example has none.
teacher.activity: Students look at pictures and write one What a ... or What ... exclamation for each, then sort them by whether they include a.

child.hook: What do you say when you see a huge mess?
child.explain: What a mess! shows how we feel. It has no action word. The words after What describe the thing.
child.play: Show a friend a picture. They shout a reaction starting with What a ... for it. Then try one without a, like What lovely weather!

checked.note: Fixed: curious summary no longer calls the pattern a noun phrase after what or a strong feeling; the body no longer singles out a (this dictionary allows a or an) and ties a to the What a mess! example; teacher explain says nominal, not nominal head. Also fixed (unflagged): 'the entry' wording; child play wording. Second round: fixed teacher.terms, cutting Exclamation is the traditional name (the entry makes no claim about traditional names).
